channel.title: Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (RCFP) – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (RCFP) – Bias and Credibility (rcfp.org)

item.title: Florida newsroom’s lawsuit forces Village of Key Biscayne to permanently scrap ‘gag’ policy
item.description: The Key Biscayne Independent, represented by RCFP attorneys, challenged the constitutionality of the policy.

item.title: Trump executive order targeting NPR, PBS is unconstitutional, judge rules
item.description: “This ruling affirms that the government cannot use its power to punish reporting that it does not like,” said RCFP’s Lisa Zycherman.

item.title: Russia’s designation of International Women’s Media Foundation as 'undesirable' is a 'blatant' attack on press freedom
item.description: "We stand in solidarity with our colleagues at the IWMF and call on the Russian government to reverse this designation.”

item.title: Journalist’s lawsuit prompts FAA to abandon no fly zone near DHS vehicles
item.description: The FAA dropped the drone restrictions after RCFP attorneys sued the agency on behalf of photojournalist Rob Levine.

item.title: RCFP attorney defends Louisiana journalist sued by local government over public records requests
item.description: “This is a meritless attempt to deter reporting,” said RCFP’s Louisiana-based staff attorney, Virginia Hamrick.

item.title: DOJ blocks public and press from accessing immigration courts, lawsuit alleges
item.description: Immigration courts should be open to the public and the press, but too often they are not, RCFP's Renee Griffin writes.

item.title: Journalists say unprecedented FBI raid on reporter’s home will have ‘widespread ramifications’
item.description: An RCFP survey of more than a dozen journalists found the raid is already impacting their ability to get important stories to the public.

item.title: The Guardian: Most immigrants targeted for deportation in 2025 had no criminal history, data reveal
item.description: The data, which The Guardian obtained with free legal support from RCFP attorneys, undercuts the government’s claim that it is targeting “dangerous criminals.”

item.title: RCFP expands free legal support to local newsrooms in Gulf states and upper Midwest
item.description: Expansion nearly doubles the Local Legal Initiative, building on six years of success supporting local journalism

item.title: 5 tips for making the most out of Indiana’s public records law
item.description: In advance of Sunshine Week, RCFP's Kris Cundiff shares his top tips for obtaining public records in Indiana.

item.title: Indiana unlawfully withheld execution drug purchasing records, judge rules
item.description: The judge sided with arguments made by an RCFP attorney representing the Indiana Capital Chronicle.

item.title: Journalist Marisa Kabas discusses her successful fight for bodycam videos of DOGE raid at US Institute of Peace
item.description: Through a lawsuit, RCFP attorneys helped Kabas obtain hours of police bodycam footage of the raid. Here’s what it shows.

item.title: After RCFP pushback, Colorado town settles First Amendment dispute with local newspaper
item.description: The town of Bennett, Colorado, had pulled advertising from The I-70 Scout in retaliation for its reporting.

item.title: Photojournalist challenges FAA’s ban on drone flights near DHS vehicles
item.description: RCFP attorneys are representing photojournalist Rob Levine in challenging the unconstitutional no fly zone.

item.title: ICE arrest of non-citizen journalist in Tennessee raises serious First Amendment concerns
item.description: The arrest and detention of non-citizen reporters can serve as a potent means of suppressing newsgathering and reporting.
